entrypoints.summary: A user permitted to push and run an unprotected-branch pipeline supplies CI configuration with a selected cache key and a cacheable payload file.
A later protected master pipeline restores its cache path and invokes the restored critical_binary through sh ./critical_binary.

affected_components.role: Derives cache entries; the merged diff conditionally appends a suffix based on pipeline protected-ref state.
Project CI/CD setting defaults cache separation to enabled and can disable it.

causal_paths.kind: cache-key derivation to protected job cache restoration

code_slices.fixed: Ci::Build#cache returns unmodified keys only when separated caches are disabled; otherwise it appends protected or non_protected according to pipeline.protected_ref?.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The project-level separated_caches setting is persisted with default true and exposed as a CI/CD setting.
code_slices.vulnerable: The disclosure identifies cache-key handling that did not incorporate the branch's protected status.

negative_controls: Before poisoning, the protected master job outputs critical_binary is safe.
With separated cache keys enabled, vendor validation directs checking distinct protected and non-protected key suffixes.
observability.positive_marker: The later protected master job outputs critical_binary is evil.

preconditions: The attacker can push or otherwise run a pipeline on an unprotected branch.
A protected branch has a job that restores a cacheable file and executes it.
The vulnerable deployment permits a shared cache identity across protected and unprotected refs.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A shell script payload stored as the cacheable critical_binary file under key test-master.
trigger_steps.summary: Run the unprotected feature pipeline configured with the protected job's cache key and a payload written to critical_binary.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A protected job configuration whose cache path includes critical_binary and whose script calls sh ./critical_binary.
trigger_steps.summary: Start a subsequent protected master pipeline that restores and shells the cached critical_binary.

capabilities.concept: Write a cache entry under a protected job's shared cache identity
Cause a protected CI job to restore and execute attacker-controlled cached content

impacts.concept: Code execution in protected CI job context

mitigations.concept: Partition CI cache keys by protected-ref state

impact.affected_asset: Integrity of protected CI job execution and its cached dependency/binary inputs.
impact.attacker_capability: A user who can run an unprotected-branch pipeline can cause a later protected job to execute a cache-resident attacker script.
impact.security_effect: Privilege escalation from unprotected-branch pipeline authority to arbitrary script execution in a protected CI job.

causal_trace.summary: An unprotected feature branch controlled by a developer-equivalent user configures cache key test-master and writes attacker-controlled content to critical_binary.
Cache identity did not account for whether the pipeline ref was protected, so an unprotected writer could select the cache identity consumed by a protected pipeline.
The later protected pipeline reuses the cache-resident critical_binary and executes it with sh ./critical_binary.

The report's ordered reproduction states that the protected master job changes from outputting critical_binary is safe to critical_binary is evil without a protected-branch code change, demonstrating execution of the poisoned cached script in the protected job context.

failure.operation: Protected CI job restores a shared cache entry and executes its critical_binary payload through the shell.

primary_invariant.statement: Cache entries writable from unprotected refs must not be restored and executed by protected-ref jobs.
primary_invariant.violated_because: Before separation, the cache key lacked protected-ref state, allowing a low-trust unprotected writer and high-trust protected reader to alias one cache entry.

quality.review_notes: The official GitLab-hosted disclosure supplies a concrete ordered two-branch reproduction and reported job-output observations; this extraction did not independently execute it. The inspected merged commit is a follow-up that makes separation configurable, rather than evidence of the initial 14.10.1 security-release commit. Separation defaults to enabled but can be disabled, so mitigation is conditional on that setting remaining enabled. Claims of secret exposure or final-product backdooring are not recorded as demonstrated impacts because they depend on protected-job permissions and behavior.

remediation.invariant_restored: When separated caches are enabled, Ci::Build#cache appends protected or non_protected according to pipeline.protected_ref?, preventing protected and unprotected jobs from resolving the same derived cache key.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Choose the predictable protected-job cache key from an unprotected branch and write a script as critical_binary to the configured cache path.
data_structure_invariants: Cache namespace resolution must include the protected-ref trust domain when cache content can cross pipeline runs.
A protected job must not consume executable cache content written by an unprotected job.
state_context.state_machine: An unprotected pipeline writes cache state; a later protected pipeline restores that persistent state and executes a file within it.

affected_versions_or_commits.value: The disclosure was filed as GitLab issue #330047 (created 2021-05-05; closed 2022-05-03). Exact affected release versions are not supplied.

target.component: CI/CD cache-key construction for build jobs

oracle.expected_negative: With cache separation enabled, protected and unprotected pipelines resolve differently suffixed keys, so the unprotected cache write is not reused by the protected job.
oracle.expected_positive: With the vulnerable shared key arrangement, after the unprotected pipeline writes its payload, a later protected master pipeline outputs critical_binary is evil.
